content: Two co-chairs with expertise in managing group processes and interpreting evidence were appointed at the start of the consultation, and their nomination was approved by the guideline development group. Members of the WHO Secretariat were present throughout the meeting to provide guidance on the overall process, but they did not have voting rights or veto power. In accordance with the rules outlined in the WHO Basic Documents and the WHO Handbook for Guideline Development, all experts participating in WHO meetings were required to declare any relevant interests prior to their involvement. The responsible technical officer and relevant departments reviewed these declarations of interest before finalizing the composition of the guideline development group and inviting members to attend the meetings. All members of the guideline development group and participants in the meetings submitted a declaration-of-interest form along with their curriculum vitae before each meeting. Participants attended in their individual capacity, not as representatives of their institutions. Additionally, they verbally declared any potential conflicts of interest at the beginning of each meeting. The management of competing interests strictly adhered to WHO guidelines for declarations of interest. Dr. Beverley-Ann Biggs disclosed that the University of Melbourne received funding from the National Health and Medical Research Council and the Australian Research Council for research on intermittent iron and folic acid supplementation during pregnancy. This research was conducted in collaboration with several institutions. It was determined that she could fully participate in the deliberations and decision-making for this guideline. Dr. Luz Maria De-Regil declared that her current employer, an international non-governmental organization focused on improving micronutrient status among vulnerable populations, is primarily funded by the Canadian government. She disclosed her and her organization’s interests in micronutrient interventions. While she participated in discussions related to iron supplementation recommendations, she recused herself from voting on this guideline. Dr. Lynnette Neufeld disclosed that her employer had received funding in the past four years for research and programming related to iron supplementation. Although she is not currently leading any of these initiatives, she had previously commissioned research on iron supplementation in a prior role. She disclosed her and her organization’s interests in micronutrient interventions. She participated in deliberations but recused herself from voting on recommendations related to iron supplementation. Dr. Héctor Bourges Rodríguez declared his role as chair of the executive board of the Danone Institute in Mexico, a non-profit organization promoting nutrition research and funded by Danone Mexico. It was agreed that he could fully participate in the deliberations and decision-making for this guideline. All other members verbally declared their interests, which were deemed irrelevant to the guideline on iron supplementation in adult women and adolescent girls. External resource persons also declared their interests but did not participate in deliberations or decision-making. The WHO Secretariat will continue to monitor research developments in the area of oral iron supplementation for menstruating adult women and adolescent girls in both malaria-endemic and non-malaria-endemic settings. If the guideline requires an update or if concerns arise regarding its validity, the Department of Nutrition for Health and Development will coordinate the update process following formal WHO procedures. As the guideline approaches its 10-year review period, the department, in collaboration with internal partners, will conduct a search for new evidence.
